newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsica hit by new bomb attacks.
newsitem.headline: Corsica hit by new bomb attacks.

text.p: Two new bomb attacks hit the troubled French Mediterranean island of Corsica overnight but no one was hurt, police said on Tuesday.

Both attacks were in the southern town of Bonifacio where one blast destroyed the parked car of the town's mayor while the other damaged the door to a local restaurant, police said. No one claimed responsibility for either attack.
A third bomb was found, but safely defused, outside the medical cabinet of the mayor's wife -- a doctor -- in Porto Vecchio, also in southern Corsica, police said.

The attacks came 24 hours after the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), "Historic Wing", the island's most hardline separatist group, claimed responsibility for a blast at the home of a former cabinet minister and mayor of the north Corsican town of Bastia. He was not at home and no one was hurt.
In a statement to the media, the FLNC had also claimed responsibility for 17 other attacks since early September, including the bombing of law courts, postal offices and banks.
Separatists have been waging a low-level bombing campaign on the island for the past 20 years.
